cse-2010-cs-23.approach: Read each entry condition: P1 waits while S1 = S2, P2 waits while S1 ≠ S2. The two entry conditions are complementary, and each exit hands the turn to the other process — classic strict alternation.

steps.title: Entry conditions
steps.body: P1 passes its loop only when $S1 \ne S2$; P2 passes only when $S1 = S2$. Both cannot be true at once, so both processes can never be inside together — **mutual exclusion holds**.

steps.title: What each exit does
steps.body: P1 exits with $S1 = S2$, which blocks P1 and admits P2. P2 exits with $S2 = \lnot S1$, i.e. $S1 \ne S2$, which blocks P2 and admits P1. The turn strictly alternates.

steps.title: Progress fails
steps.body: If P1 leaves its CS and P2 never wants to enter, then $S1 = S2$ stays true and P1 waits forever although the CS is free. A process outside its CS (P2) is deciding who enters, so **progress is violated**.

Mutual exclusion does hold — the two entry conditions cannot both be true.
Mutual exclusion holds, so "neither" is wrong.
Progress fails: P1 cannot re-enter unless P2 takes its turn.

pitfalls: Random initial values do not matter: whichever condition holds first, exactly one process can enter.
